text: The <highlight>whoami</highlight> command identifies the current logged-in user. Adding the <highlight>/priv</highlight> flag is the most critical step in Windows privilege escalation as it reveals hidden system 'superpowers' assigned to the account.

code:
PRIVILEGES INFORMATION
----------------------
Privilege Name                Description                          State
============================= ==================================== ========
SeChangeNotifyPrivilege       Bypass traverse checking             Enabled
SeImpersonatePrivilege        Impersonate a client...              Enabled

text: The <highlight>dir</highlight> command lists files and directories. Using the <highlight>/a</highlight> flag ensures that hidden and system files are visible, similar to <highlight>ls -la</highlight> in Linux.

code:
Directory of c:\inetpub\wwwroot

03/19/2026  06:00 AM    <DIR>          .
03/19/2026  06:00 AM    <DIR>          ..
07/25/2020  08:15 AM    <DIR>          nt4wrksv

text: To view IP addresses, subnet masks, and gateway information, use <highlight>ipconfig</highlight>. The <highlight>/all</highlight> flag provides detailed info like DNS servers and MAC addresses.

code:
Ethernet adapter Ethernet:
   Description . . . . . . . . . . . : Red Hat VirtIO Ethernet Adapter
   IPv4 Address. . . . . . . . . . . : 10.10.198.54(Preferred)

text: The <highlight>net user</highlight> command displays all local accounts. Checking a specific username reveals their group memberships (like <highlight>Administrators</highlight>) and when they last changed their password.

code:
User name                    Bob
Account active               Yes
Local Group Memberships      *Users
Global Group memberships     *None

text: In Windows CMD, <highlight>type</highlight> is used to display the contents of a text file directly in the terminal, equivalent to the Linux <highlight>cat</highlight> command.
The <highlight>where /R</highlight> command is used to recursively search for a file from a specific starting directory. This is useful for finding hidden flags or configuration files.
